group.passage: When someone in Taiwan calls 119 for help, an ambulance usually arrives within minutes. In 2017, the average wait was just under six minutes. Inside, trained workers can start caring for the patient right away. In this way, a modern ambulance is like a hospital on wheels: patients begin receiving treatment on the road, long before they reach the hospital itself. Yet the first ambulances looked very different. They began on the battlefield. Dominique Jean Larrey was a French army doctor who became the chief doctor in Napoleon's army. In his day, wounded soldiers were usually left where they fell until the fighting was over, so many waited hours or even days for help. In 1797, Larrey built special carts pulled by horses to carry the wounded away during the battle. People called them flying ambulances. His teams also cared for soldiers from both sides. Later, the idea moved from the army to the city. After the American Civil War, cities such as Cincinnati, New York, London, and Paris started their own ambulance services. In 1869, Edward Dalton, a former army doctor, set up a program in New York City. His ambulances carried bandages, splints, and a box of medicines. By around 1900, young doctors often rode along, but the drivers themselves had almost no medical training. Before long, carriages powered by electricity, steam, or gasoline began to take the place of horses. Progress did not always continue, however. After World War II, many American ambulances were really hearses, and about half were run by funeral home workers, most of whom had never taken a first-aid class. A report in 1966 showed how poor emergency care was, and the government began paying to train emergency medical technicians, or EMTs. Today, Taiwan also trains EMTs at three levels, and its fire departments send out ambulances more than a million times a year.

translation_zh.text:
在臺灣，有人撥打 119 求救時，救護車通常幾分鐘內就會抵達。2017 年，平均等待時間不到六分鐘。車上受過訓練的人員可以馬上開始照顧病人。從這一點來看，現代的救護車就像一間「有輪子的醫院」：病人在路上就開始接受治療，遠在抵達醫院之前。然而，最早的救護車看起來非常不一樣。
救護車起源於戰場。多明尼克‧尚‧賴瑞是法國的軍醫，後來成為拿破崙軍隊的首席軍醫。在他那個時代，受傷的士兵通常倒在原地，要等戰鬥結束才有人處理，所以很多人要等好幾個小時，甚至好幾天才得到救助。1797 年，賴瑞造了由馬拉的特製車輛，在戰鬥進行中就把傷兵載走。人們稱這種車為「飛行救護車」。他的團隊也照顧交戰雙方的士兵。
後來，這個構想從軍隊傳到了城市。美國南北戰爭之後，辛辛那提、紐約、倫敦和巴黎等城市開辦了自己的救護車服務。1869 年，曾任軍醫的愛德華‧道爾頓在紐約市設立了救護車計畫。他的救護車上載著繃帶、夾板和一箱藥品。到了 1900 年前後，常有年輕醫師隨車出勤，但駕駛本身幾乎沒有受過醫療訓練。不久之後，以電力、蒸汽或汽油為動力的車輛開始取代馬匹。
不過，進步並不是一路持續。二次世界大戰後，美國許多救護車其實是靈車，大約一半由葬儀社的員工經營，他們大多數從來沒上過急救課。1966 年的一份報告顯示緊急救護有多麼糟糕，政府開始出錢訓練緊急救護技術員（EMT）。今天，臺灣也把救護技術員分成三級來訓練，各地消防局的救護車一年出勤超過一百萬次。
